Pricing provisions (Section 11 Fees, Section 10 maintenance fees, Section 2 additional-location fees, Section 17 perpetuity conditioned on fee payment) simply refer to the Fee Schedule; searches for "most favoured/favourable", "best price", "other customers", "competitor" and price/rate matching language returned nothing, and the general provisions (Section 20) contain no such covenant. Sparkling therefore has no obligation to extend Garman terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers, which is the playbook's preferred position (no MFN burdening the Customer). Nothing to redline; we would of course welcome a Garman-granted MFN in our favour if it can be negotiated.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering all employees, so we have narrowed this to a mutual non-solicitation of personnel directly involved in the services for twelve months after their involvement ends, with the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. This reflects our playbook fallback position on restrictive covenants.

ops.newText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of the relevant individual's involvement in the provision of services under this Agreement, neither party shall directly solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement. This Section does not restrict either party from hiring any person, and does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or to any person who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis or in response to such general advertisement.

proposal.summary: Convert the mutual no-hire covering all employees into a 12-month non-solicitation limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

quote: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 19 binds us as well as the vendor, and it is a no-hire ("agree not to hire ... any employee of the other party"), not a non-solicit. It also reaches all employees of the other party, not just personnel involved in the services, extends to affiliates, and has no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions and restrictions covering all vendor personnel are walk-away items under the rule, so this fails the fallback on material terms notwithstanding the acceptable 12-month tail. Because the mutual structure is already part of the bargain, we narrowed to the fallback rather than deleting the clause outright: mutual solicitation-only restriction, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and data return/deletion obligation as Section 17(d)

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
rationale: Section 17 addresses post-termination effects in one direction only: Sparkling must cease use and return or destroy Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes, and on Garman default the license converts to perpetual with a refund of prepaid fees. Nothing anywhere in the Agreement obliges Garman to return Sparkling's data (which Garman handles under Section 4(b) data conversion and in the course of maintenance and support) or to provide any exit or migration assistance; the survival list in Section 18 contains no such obligation, and the Section 16 escrow/on-site Codes only address software continuity, not data return. The rule's fallback (90 days of assistance plus data export within 30 days) is therefore unmet, so we inserted the preferred position as a new Section 17(d): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter.
